entities.summary:
Willibald was a 8th-century bishop of Eichstätt in Bavaria, Germany.

Born into a Frankish family, Willibald rose to prominence as Bishop of Eichstätt from 766 until his death in 786. He played a key role in the preservation and translation of classical texts during the Carolingian Renaissance, which had a lasting impact on Western education and culture.

Willibald was a close associate of Charlemagne, who appointed him as the chief advisor for ecclesiastical affairs in Bavaria. This partnership led to significant reforms within the Catholic Church and the establishment of new monastic schools, which helped spread learning throughout Europe.

In his legacy, Willibald is remembered as a devoted servant of Christ and a champion of education and intellectual pursuits. His efforts during the Carolingian Renaissance cemented his place in history as a pivotal figure in shaping Western civilization.
